answer: Cross-epoch reward fingerprint matching. Each epoch, record the distribution of reward categories an identity claims; require the next epoch’s profile to stay within a bounded divergence of its own history. A cloned identity must split its nectar across many profiles, making each shallow and inconsistent. Divergence beyond threshold freezes payouts pending review, and rebuilding a believable history costs repeated genuine participation, not a one-time fee. This mirror of past behaviour makes each viable island of activity expensive to fake at scale.
